caption: Pairwise relation between the three evaluation axes across the 18 E2-A runs. Each point is one run; colour identifies the architecture and marker shape its family. (a) Internal test versus the Pandian2019 external domain. (b) Internal test versus the PlantVillage external domain. (c) The two external domains against each other. No panel shows a monotonic trend and none of the three Spearman coefficients reaches significance: no axis predicts the others.

Per-architecture performance in both external domains and rank reversal across axes. (a) Rust recall on Pandian2019 and (b) macro-F1 on the two PlantVillage classes without provenance overlap. Filled points are seeds 17, 42 and 73; the vertical tick marks the mean and the open circle the minimum across the three runs. (c) Merit rank of each architecture on the three axes, with Pandian2019 abbreviated to Pandian; crossing lines indicate that the order does not carry over. EfficientNet-B0 ranks first internally, second on Pandian2019 and last on PlantVillage; Swin-Tiny ranks last internally and first on PlantVillage.

Destination of the 1,922 rust images of the Pandian2019 external domain, one row per run. Cell values are the proportion of images assigned to each class; cells at or above 0.20 are annotated. The dashed green box marks the correct class and the solid orange box the class that absorbs the error. The healthy class is the dominant erroneous destination in all 18 runs, reaching 0.81 for ResNet50 with seed 73.

Destination of the 1,498 leaf blight and gray leaf spot images of the PlantVillage external domain, one row per run, averaged over the two classes. Cell values, annotation threshold and box coding follow Fig. 3. Here the rust class absorbs the error in 26 of the 36 class-by-run cases, whereas healthy dominates in only one: the sink is a property of the domain-class pair rather than of the model. ResNet50 with seed 17 is the single run whose dominant destination is grasshopper.

Reliability diagram on the internal test for seed 17 of the six architectures. Bins contain an equal number of observations (10 bins, about 172 images each) so that no point reflects sampling noise; the expected calibration error quoted in the text uses the standard 15 equal-width bins. The lower panel shows the confidence distribution. All curves lie above the diagonal, indicating underconfidence: observed accuracy exceeds stated confidence. The pattern holds in all 18 runs, in which the signed calibration error was negative. Temperature scaling with T = 0.54 reduces the mean expected calibration error from 0.168 to 0.008 without altering the arg max class, and therefore leaves recall unchanged.
